faqs.question: What is Labomatic's Industrial Liquid Chromatography system used for?
faqs.answer: Labomatic's Industrial Liquid Chromatography systems are used for industrial-scale process and production purification. They're engineered for high-throughput, continuous separation in pharmaceutical and chemical industry settings.

faqs.question: What is the HD-5000 pump and why does it anchor the system?
faqs.answer: The HD-5000 is Labomatic's three-piston HPLC gradient pump, and it anchors the platform because it includes an integrated system controller for method programming and control of the complete HPLC system.

faqs.question: What flow rate and pressure does the HD-5000 support?
faqs.answer: The HD-5000 pump system supports flow rates from 5 to 4920 mL/min, with pressures up to 600 bar (8700 psi).

faqs.question: Can the HD-5000 run complex gradients?
faqs.answer: Yes, the HD-5000 supports binary through quaternary gradient formation, in both high-pressure and low-pressure configurations, with an active mixing system for low-pressure gradients.

faqs.question: How many pumps and valves can one system controller manage?
faqs.answer: A single HD-5000 system controller can manage 12 or more pump mechanisms and up to 20 valves, whether static or pulsed.

faqs.question: What other components make up a full Labomatic system?
faqs.answer: A complete system typically includes LABOPORT valves and sample injection systems, LABOCORD detectors (UV/VIS, DAD, RI, or MS), the LABOCOL Vario 4000 fraction collector series, and LABOCHROM 5 software.

faqs.question: Is an ATEX-compliant or GMP version available?
faqs.answer: Yes, Labomatic offers fully custom system configurations, including ATEX-compliant GMP system solutions for hazardous-area or regulated production environments.

faqs.question: Can the HD-5000 handle buffer eluents?
faqs.answer: Yes, active piston back-flushing is built into the HD-5000, allowing buffer eluents to be used without the typical complications they can introduce.

faqs.answer: Pricing depends on the specific pump, valve, detector, and compliance configuration developed for your process. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your requirements are confirmed with Labomatic.

body.text: The platform is built around the LABOMATIC HD-5000 three-piston HPLC gradient pump, which comes with an integrated system controller for method programming and control of the complete HPLC system.
Flow rates span 5 to 4920 mL/min across the HD-5000 pump range, with pressures up to 600 bar (8700 psi).
The pump uses a three-piston system built around primary and secondary pistons, and five different pump heads are available, which can also be combined with one another to match a specific process.
Gradient formation runs from binary through quaternary, in both high-pressure and low-pressure configurations, with an active mixing system supporting low-pressure gradients specifically.
Active piston back-flushing is built in, allowing buffer eluents to be used without the complications they typically introduce.
A single system controller can manage 12 or more pump mechanisms and up to 20 valves, whether static or pulsed, alongside flow or constant-pressure operation modes.
Dosing precision reaches the microliter level, useful for additives like DEA or TFA that need to be introduced in exact, small quantities.

Beyond the pump, a standard system draws on LABOPORT system switching valves and sample injection systems, LABOCORD detectors (UV/VIS, DAD, RI, or MS), the LABOCOL Vario 4000 fraction collector series, and LABOCHROM 5 software to run the whole process.
Systems are available in a standard configuration, or fully customized, including ATEX-compliant GMP system solutions for regulated or hazardous production environments.

sections.title: The HD-5000 Pump System
sections.tabSummary: Pump head combinations, dosing, and multi-valve control
body: This section covers the HD-5000's pump head combinations, dosing precision, and multi-valve control capability.
The HD-5000 sits at the center of every Labomatic Industrial LC system, and its flexibility is what allows the same core platform to scale across very different production needs.

Its three-piston design, built around primary and secondary pistons, delivers a nearly pulsation-free flow across a wide range, from 5 mL/min at the low end up to 4920 mL/min, at pressures reaching 600 bar. Five different pump heads are available, and they can be combined with one another rather than locking you into a single fixed configuration. Gradient elution goes all the way up to quaternary, in either high-pressure or low-pressure form, with an active mixing system supporting the low-pressure side specifically. Active piston back-flushing keeps buffer eluents genuinely usable, avoiding the fouling issues they can otherwise cause. From a single system controller, the HD-5000 can manage 12 or more pump mechanisms and up to 20 valves, static or pulsed, while also supporting microliter-precision dosing for additives like DEA or TFA.

groups.title: Building a Complete System
groups.summary: How pumps, valves, detectors, and software come together
groups.description: This section covers how pumps, valves, detectors, and software combine into a full Labomatic Industrial LC system.
body: The HD-5000 pump is the core, but a working industrial LC system needs the rest of the ecosystem around it, and Labomatic builds that ecosystem to work together natively.

LABOPORT system switching valves and sample injection systems handle flow routing and sample introduction. LABOCORD detectors round out detection with UV/VIS, DAD, RI, or MS options depending on what your compounds require. Fraction collection runs through the LABOCOL Vario 4000 series, and the entire process is programmed and monitored through LABOCHROM 5 software. All of it can be delivered as a standard configuration, or built out as a fully custom system, including ATEX-compliant GMP solutions where regulated or hazardous-area production demands it.
